Subject: Cardea Order Form redlines — defense scope & insurance offset

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for sending the draft order form. Legal has reviewed the indemnity section and has pushed back on two items that are blockers for our procurement team:

1) Defense control: Your proposed language gives Redwood sole control of the defense for third-party IP claims. Cardea needs the ability to appoint counsel and direct the defense when Cardea reasonably believes the claim could affect its product roadmap or reputational exposure.

2) Insurance offset: The redline attempts to allow Redwood to reduce its indemnity obligation by insurance proceeds. Cardea agrees to an insurance offset in principle, but we need clearer limits — specifically a cap tied to the policy limits and a carveout that prevents Redwood from offsetting amounts that Cardea is required to indemnify its customers for.

I've attached our redlines (Cardea_OrderForm_redlines_20250515.pdf). Can your team propose language that preserves Cardea's right to participate in and, in certain circumstances, control the defense, while also resolving the insurance-offset mechanics? Procurement would like to close the order form this month.

If you prefer, we can get our counsel and yours on a short call early next week.

Thanks,

Marta Lopez
Sr. Contracts Manager
Cardea Systems

Marta —

Appreciate the clear notes and the redlines. I pulled in Laura (sales lead on this account) and Aditya (legal counsel) so we can propose a clean counter. Quick summary of where we think we can land:

- Defense control: we can accept a joint-defense approach for third-party IP claims where Cardea may select counsel if the claim specifically implicates Cardea's product branding or data use. For claims solely about Redwood's model outputs or model IP, Redwood would retain defense control. We can draft objective trigger language (e.g., "claims that primarily allege use of Cardea-branded integrations or Cardea data subjects") to avoid ambiguity.

- Insurance offset: Redwood won't use insurer recoveries to avoid payment of amounts that Cardea is contractually required to pay its downstream customers. We are willing to limit the offset to net recoveries after defense costs and to a cap equal to Redwood's total indemnity exposure under the order form (not the broader MSA).

I've asked Aditya to put a drafted counterproposal in the attached PDF (Redwood_Counterproposal_Defense-v2.pdf). Key asks from our side: a short joint-notice period for claims (7 business days) and cooperation rights for both sides.

Can Cardea review the proposed language and let us know if that narrows to a close? If helpful, we can set a 30-minute counsel-to-counsel call Monday noon PT.

Cheers,

Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Hi Marta —

Aditya here from Redwood Legal. Thanks for the suggested language — it’s precise and helpful. We can accept the proposed "solely Redwood model IP" test as a bright-line for defense control, with two implementation clarifications:

1) The test will be applied at notice intake based on the claim allegations; if later factual developments show a different primary allegation (e.g., Cardea data is implicated), the parties will meet to agree on reallocation and, if needed, transition of defense control.

2) Insurance offset will be limited to net recoveries after defense costs, and Redwood will not seek to reduce indemnity payments that Cardea is contractually obligated to make to its customers. We will add an explicit example to the order form to make the offset mechanics operational.

I'll put redline language into the HubSpot deal record and upload a marked PDF to the DocuSign packet prior to Monday's call. Meeting confirmed for Monday 12:00 PT. Dial-in and link here: https://meet.redwood.ai/meeting/CRD-1143 (counsel-only).
